fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the front of the residence without obstruction.
• Trim any shrubs or low branches along the walkway that could slow responder movement toward the front door.
• Mark or unlock any gate or passage that connects the front of the property to the rear so responders are not blocked when the single front access point is congested.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around both buildings without obstruction.
• Keep the area between the main residence and detached structure clear so responders can use it as a staging or movement path.
• Post the property address visibly on both the street side and, if possible, near the detached structure so responders can orient themselves on the property.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang close to or over the structure to reduce the chance of fire reaching the roof.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between the trees and the building.
• Cut or mow grass close to the structure, keeping it short during dry periods.
• Remove shrubs growing directly next to the structure or any attached features such as decks or fences.
• Separate shrub clusters near the structure so they do not form a continuous line of plants leading toward the building.
• Keep the single access route clear of low-hanging branches and overgrown vegetation along both sides so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mow or cut tall grass along the edges of the driveway to reduce the chance of fire blocking the access route.
• Remove any dead grass, dead shrubs, or dry plant debris that has accumulated next to the structure or outbuildings.
